rows.what the ink shows: Four letter events follow op.: a small initial open c, a descending p-shaped stroke, a separate broad open c bowl, and the terminal taller t with a rightward foot. The separate second c between p and t favors cpct over cpt.

The full deleted phrase is crossed by a dense horizontal stroke; small upright tips and lower hooks survive, but the proposed a-i-s-é bodies cannot be separated reliably. No distinct acute can be assigned to a final e through the overstrike, so the whole word remains uncertain.

A low rho-like hook, a tiny lower notch, and two curved parentheses survive the horizontal deletion; inside, two short upper tips merge with the strike. The notch does not establish an index at all, the interior does not settle joined uv versus one w-shaped letter, and the adjacent cancelled run leaves the full expression endpoint uncertain; the entire source unsure span is retained.

unresolved_components.index: Presence or absence remains uncertain; if present, 1 versus i is unresolved.
unresolved_components.argument: Joined uv versus a single w-shaped letter remains unresolved.
unresolved_components.extent: Continuation into the adjacent cancelled run cannot be established or excluded.

rows.what the ink shows: The proposed words lie in a crossed region above/right of the rho formula: short horizontal remnants precede a tall hooked/descending stroke and a long doubled rightward trace. Cancellation and the large surrounding deletion line prevent separating all of c-e and q-u-i, including any i dot.

The crossed two-letter unit has a tall looped E with an open lower return, followed by a separate shorter upright t stem. Two horizontal cancellation strokes pass across their middle, but both baseline letter bodies remain distinguishable.

The first of the two baseline letters is tall and filled, with a closed narrow lower turn and high right return; the second is lower, with an open rounded trough, rising shoulder and rightward tail. At original contrast these match the separate v and u, respectively, in the right-hand factors of (24); the closing parenthesis and raised star are distinct.

Inside the second starred parenthesis, the first baseline letter has the returned upright and trough of u; the following letter is a simpler open cup with a rising right stroke, v. Both baseline letters precede the separate closing parenthesis and raised star; the cancellation line crosses their lower portions.

The cluster retains an upper left-pointing angle and a separate short lower horizontal bar, supporting ≤. Thick cancellation strokes obscure part of the lower/right edge; the following equals sign is separate and outside this mark.

A tall initial f with a low loop is visible, followed by connected low strokes and a pointed terminal rise under the deletion. The intervening o/r/m shapes and an abbreviation point cannot be separated reliably, so the full asserted form. remains uncertain.

The outer curved/slanting strokes enclose a p with a descending loop, a low r shoulder, a small rounded o, and a second p with a lower return, followed by a separate upright 1. A horizontal deletion crosses all of them, but both parentheses and the letter/numeral sequence remain distinguishable; no distinct abbreviation point is established.

The complete word has a tall initial f, a small adjoining curved stroke, and two extended low dark groups before the following comma-like stroke. Neither a c/t crossing and abbreviation point, the full tions ending, nor separate r/m/e/s strokes can be distinguished; all three source candidates remain open after full-word color and grayscale enlargements.
